source_evidence: Verified local HEAD and GitHub PR #49 head are both 0ba321eace06bd809e3d9ca89934fb27bd185751; the exact-head diff changes only service_visits.py and its focused test.

service_visit now derives buffered from the deep-copied observed producer input and bounds delivery with min(200, need, spendable inventory, max(0, catalog stack size minus buffered)); therefore a 50-item stack observed with 5 iron ore cannot request more than 45 additional ore.

Executed an isolated read-only planner scenario matching the changed test: 50-stack iron ore, 5 buffered, 80 carried, target 100. It produced a paid factory_insert quantity of 45, remained allowed, and left the original observed input unchanged.

The native factory transfer still requires the actor to be able to reach the machine, verifies target.get_insertable_count(item) before removal, takes items from the character main inventory, refunds an incomplete insertion, and records a receipt only for the native transfer.

The fairness implementation is outside the exact-head diff and retains its connected original-character, game.speed == 1, and cheat_mode false assertions; walking uses a native requested path and walking_state, while mining independently requires native reach and observes inventory gain rather than granting items.
